summary: Token-bucket reset cascade causing elevated 5xx and runtime OOMs during connection surge
description:
Issue summary: Between 2026-03-01 09:12 and 09:40 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503) for a subset of requests from customer CodaMaps. The spike coincided with a short-lived connection surge from a client-side campaign. API gateway logs show token-bucket counters resetting unexpectedly, which permitted a rapid microburst of requests. The burst amplified retries and pushed serving runtimes into rapid connection churn and OOMs, producing cascading 5xx responses across a small set of dedicated shards.

Impact: CodaMaps reported ~28% of requests returning 5xx during the window; increased tail latency and failed streaming sessions. Customer affected on their dedicated pool (dedicated tier) in us-east. Business impact: degraded user-facing search experiences for ~30 minutes and multiple reconnects for streaming widgets.

Environment: Production (prod-us-east) — Dedicated capacity pool for CodaMaps. Models affected primarily redwood-rlhf-13b for chat and open-mistral-7b for short text completions. Autoscaler configured with min 3 / max 20 nodes for the tenant.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Client-side campaign generated a burst of ~2.2k concurrent requests over a 2-minute window.
2) API gateway rate-limiter token buckets for the tenant appeared to reset (bucket refill logic returned to full) after a transient datastore timeout.
3) Gateways forwarded a microburst to the load balancer and serving-runtime.
4) Serving runtime began hitting elevated memory pressure; some pods reported OOMKilled and restarted.
5) Client retries (exponential backoff not enforced in one SDK version) amplified load during restarts, resulting in continued 502/503 responses.

Observed logs & metrics:
- gateway.log excerpt [09:13:07]: "token_bucket: refill_on_error=true bucket_state=full after_datastore_timeout"
- lb.metrics: "requests_per_sec tenant=CodaMaps spike 2.2k -> 3.1k concurrent"
- runtime pod (node-17): "OOMKilled: rss 12.9G > limit 12G"; multiple restarts within 60s.
- apigw responses: surge of 502/503 with increased 5xx ratio from baseline 0.3% -> 28%
- monitoring alert: rate-limiter datastore timeout (Redis) 09:12:55 - 09:14:05

Additional context: CodaMaps is on a dedicated pool with pinned shards; the autoscaler did initiate scale-up but warm-up time and container start latency prevented immediate capacity relief. SDK version used by the customer contains a retry policy that does not jitter, which worsened retry amplification.
comments: 2026-03-01 09:25 - CodaMaps (support@codamaps.example): We're seeing a lot of 502s during a scheduled campaign, can you confirm service status?
2026-03-01 09:28 - Support (Asha Patel): Investigating; initial signals indicate elevated 5xx, collecting logs and metrics. Will update within 30 minutes.

2026-03-01 09:40 - SRE (Miguel Santos): Found token-bucket refill events aligned with Redis timeout. Some runtime pods OOMKilled; autoscaler initiated but slow. Temporarily throttling client level for CodaMaps to reduce retries (manual mitigation applied).
2026-03-01 10:05 - CodaMaps: Thanks — we deployed a client-side patch to add jitter and reduced concurrency. Errors falling but want root cause and long-term fix.

2026-03-02 11:12 - Eng (Priya Nair): Reproduced locally with synthetic burst against a local Redis in failure-mode; token-bucket reset occurs when refill RPC returns error and fallback logic sets bucket to full. Preparing PR to change fallback to 'no refill' and add telemetry.
2026-03-03 14:20 - Support (Asha Patel): Notifying customer of planned fix and timeline. Collecting post-incident notes and runbook updates.
investigation_notes: 09:30 - Initial triage: correlated 5xx spikes with a Redis client timeout used by rate-limiter (token bucket state persisted in Redis).
09:45 - Confirmed that refill-on-error code path sets bucket to full instead of leaving it unchanged; this allows a sudden burst after transient failure.

09:50 - Observed multiple runtime pods with rapid memory growth traced to KV cache thrash when handling concurrent fanout requests; OOMs occurred on nodes with older kernel memory reclamation behavior.
10:10 - Autoscaler scaled from 3 -> 9 nodes but container init (model warm-up + quant kernels) took ~45s; not fast enough to absorb microburst.
11:30 - Customer SDK lacks jitter on retry causing synchronized retry waves; recommended immediate client-side jitter patch which customer applied.

2026-03-02 - Engineering reproduced token-bucket reset in a test harness. Verified a code path in api-gateway's rate-limiter where datastore errors trigger a full refill as a fail-open defense. Determined fail-open is unsafe for dedicated pools; change to fail-closed with metric and scrubbed logs.
2026-03-02 - Observability gap: we didn't have tenant-level token-bucket refill events surfaced in dashboards. Adding metric and alert for refill-on-error counts.
2026-03-03 - Cross-team sync: SRE, Gateway, Runtime, and Customer Success to coordinate rollout of fix and updated runbook.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-01 09:44): temporary tenant-level throttling rule added for CodaMaps at the API gateway to limit concurrent active connections and reduce retry amplification.
Customer action: CodaMaps deployed SDK patch (added exponential backoff + jitter) at 09:55 which reduced synchronized retries and helped restore normal traffic patterns.

Short-term fix (2026-03-02): updated gateway config to change refill-on-error behavior from 'refill full' -> 'do not alter bucket on datastore error' (fail-closed). Deployed to prod-us-east on a canary subset of gateways and monitored metrics for 1h before wider rollout.

Long-term fix (planned): PR #2984 to change rate-limiter fallback behavior, add per-tenant refill-on-error metrics, and ensure runbook includes steps to apply tenant-level soft-throttles. Also add autoscaler warm-up optimization doc to reduce model init latency for dedicated pools.

Post-incident changes: new alert rule for 'token_bucket_refill_on_error > 10/min for tenant' and dashboard panel for tenant-level refill events; runbook updated with exact mitigation commands and escalation path.

Status: Affects mitigated; engineering change in rollout. Customer satisfied with workaround and request for postmortem and preventative recommendations. Follow-up action item created: INT-3302 (implement autoscaler pre-warm for pinned shards).
